newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia avg lending rate lifted 80 bps to 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia avg lending rate lifted 80 bps to 10.4 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate rose 80 basis points to 10.4 percent on Wednesday, lifted by the high volume of term loans on the money market.
Dealers put the day's trade at 52.4 million kuna, against demand for 57.6 million. Almost 14 million kuna of the total was accounted for by old deals renewed by lenders.
Interbank rates remained stable to firmer at call money 8.0-percent rate and 10.5-12, charged for up to 10-day funds. One- to three-month rates ranged between 15 and 18 percent.
Insurers rolled over one-month loans at 13 and two-month at 14 percent.
The central bank intervened in money supply by buying a large amount of German marks and dollars from the banking sector. It will release kuna to banks in two days' time.

It calculated the kuna midrates for Thursday's dealings weaker at 6.2859 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5679 to the mark after the intervention. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
